readerTitle: Why a booking platform can earn once and then disappear
caseNote: 가상 사례 (청소 예약 플랫폼, 앱 아이디어 3개) + 실제 연구 (Levitt & Syverson, 부동산 중개인)
insight: 수수료는 거래가 일어날 때마다 내가 그 자리에 꼭 필요할 때만 계속 들어온다. 반복되는 단순한 관계에서는 고객과 공급자가 나를 건너뛴다.
misconception: 거래를 연결해 주면 그 뒤의 거래에서도 계속 수수료를 받을 수 있다. 거래량이 늘면 수수료 수익도 따라 는다.

sources.text: Levitt, S. D. & Syverson, C. (2008). Market Distortions When Agents Are Better Informed: The Value of Information in Real Estate Transactions. Review of Economics and Statistics, 90(4).
청소 플랫폼과 앱 아이디어는 설명용 가상 사례

factChecks.note: Levitt & Syverson(2008): 중개인 본인 소유 주택이 약 3.7% 더 비싸게, 시장에 약 9.5일 더 오래 있다가 팔렸다는 결과. 게시 전 원문 수치를 다시 확인하세요. 카드에는 "about 4%"와 "more than a week longer"로 적었습니다.
연구 대상은 미국 시카고 지역 주택 거래입니다. 카드에는 특정 국가의 중개 수수료율을 적지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Why a booking platform can earn once and then disappear
body: A new platform matches homeowners with house cleaners and keeps 20% of each booking. Customers love it. Ratings are great.
Yet three months in, the founder notices something odd. New customers keep arriving, but almost none of them book a second time.

image.label: Cleaner and homeowner swapping phone numbers at the door
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 현관에서 청소 도우미와 집주인이 웃으며 휴대폰을 맞대 연락처를 교환하는 장면. 뒤쪽 벽에 걸린 태블릿 화면의 예약 앱이 쓸쓸하게 꺼져 가는 느낌. 실제 앱 로고 사용 금지.

cards.title: Your best customers stop booking through you.
body: You run the cleaning platform. After a good first clean, many customers simply call the cleaner directly and pay in cash.

options.text: Raise the commission to 30% to make more from each first booking
options.feedback: You earn more per first visit, but you give both sides an even bigger reason to leave right after it.

options.text: Ban sharing contact details and fine cleaners who take clients off the platform
options.feedback: Rules slow the leak a little, but they're hard to enforce in someone's home and they annoy the cleaners you need.

options.text: Make every repeat booking worth paying for: insurance, easy rescheduling, backup cleaners, payment handled
options.feedback: This costs you money to build, but it gives both sides a reason to keep you in the middle of every visit.

cards.title: One customer, one year.
body: The platform did the hard part: finding a trusted cleaner. Then it was paid for **one visit** out of fifty.

cards.title: Commissions
body: A **commission** is a share of each deal you help make happen. No deal, no fee.
That's why sellers like it. They pay only when they earn, so it's easy to sign them up. And your income grows as their sales grow.
But there's a catch hidden in the definition: you're paid per deal, so you must be needed *for each deal*, not just the first one.

image.label: A middleman figure standing between buyer and seller, taking a slice of each coin
image.brief: 인포그래픽. 왼쪽 구매자, 오른쪽 판매자, 가운데 중개자. 동전이 지나갈 때마다 중개자가 작은 조각을 떼어 감. 아래쪽에 두 번째, 세 번째 동전이 중개자를 우회해 위로 직접 넘어가는 점선 화살표.

cards.title: Commissions thrive when each deal needs you again.
body: Commissions work best where deals are rare, large or risky:
list: **Rare:** people sell a house a few times in their life, so there's no repeat relationship to take elsewhere
**Large:** a small share of a big deal still pays well
**Risky:** strangers need someone to hold the payment, check quality or handle disputes
cards.callout: Weekly cleaning is frequent, small and low-risk after the first visit. That's the worst fit.
cards.softwareNote: App stores and resale marketplaces keep their commissions because each purchase runs through their payment, delivery and refunds. A freelancer platform faces the cleaner problem: once a client trusts a developer, they're tempted to work together directly.

cards.title: A commission also shapes the agent's behavior.
body: Whoever earns the commission is paid for closing, not for the best result.

Economists Steven Levitt and Chad Syverson studied home sales and found that agents' own houses sold for about 4% more and stayed on the market more than a week longer than clients' homes. A slightly higher price adds little to the agent's cut, but waiting costs them time.
So when you design or pay a commission, ask what it rewards.

cards.title: Three app ideas. Which suits a commission?
body: You're choosing which marketplace app to build, and you want to earn a commission on each deal.

options.text: An app for booking the same dog walker every weekday
options.feedback: Easy to launch, but it's the cleaning story again: frequent, local and simple, so owners and walkers soon skip you.

options.text: A marketplace for used pro camera gear, with checked listings and held payment
options.feedback: Each sale is one-off, valuable and risky between strangers. Your checks and held payment are worth paying for every single time.

options.text: A platform matching companies with freelance developers for long projects
options.feedback: The deals are big, but trust builds over months and clients may go direct. You'd need ongoing value, like contracts and payments, to keep earning.

cards.title: A commission lasts only as long as you stay useful in each deal.
body: Before choosing commissions, ask whether buyers and sellers would still need you on their tenth deal together.
**Try it today:** list where your money comes from. For any fee you take on deals, write down what you do that the two sides can't easily do without you.
